title: OIDC Implicit Flow
subtitle: DEPRECATED — kept for recognizing and migrating legacy integrations. The IdP returns tokens directly in the URL fragment with no code exchange and no client authentication; use Authorization Code + PKCE instead.

steps.label: Open the SPA
steps.lede: The user loads a single-page app. The SPA generates state and nonce, then redirects to the IdP asking for tokens to be returned directly — no back-channel code exchange.
steps.devtools: ⛔ Deprecated flow — this walkthrough is for auditing legacy implicit integrations; new work should use Authorization Code + PKCE. Open DevTools (F12) → Network, enable Preserve log (the authorize response redirects). The tell is response_type=id_token token.

steps.label: Redirect to /authorize
steps.lede: The browser is redirected to the authorization endpoint requesting id_token token. nonce is required — in implicit it is the ONLY replay defense. The IdP returns the tokens in the redirect URL fragment.
steps.devtools: Filter on authorize. Confirm response_type=id_token token, state, and the required nonce. The 302 Location carries the tokens after # — the fragment. Note there is no /token call and no client authentication anywhere in this flow.

steps.label: Callback loads — fragment NOT sent to server
steps.lede: The callback page loads. Critically, the browser does NOT send the fragment to the server, so this request carries no token data. The SPA reads the tokens from location.hash in JavaScript instead.

jwt.title: Decoded id_token (carries at_hash)
payload: Must match — the ONLY replay defense in implicit

steps.devtools: The callback request shows no token data — the fragment never reached the server. Read the tokens from the address bar, the authorize row’s Location header, or location.hash in the Console. That any script can read location.hash is exactly the leakage problem. Decode the id_token and confirm nonce matches and at_hash is present.

steps.label: Verify state, validate id_token + at_hash
steps.lede: The SPA parses the fragment, strips it from the URL, verifies state, and fully validates the id_token (JWKS signature, iss, aud, exp, nonce). It also checks at_hash to bind the access token that arrived alongside it.
steps.devtools: Not a network event. With no back-channel exchange, nonce is the only replay protection and at_hash is the only binding between the ID token and the access token. A nonce mismatch means a replayed/injected id_token — reject.

steps.label: Call the API with the access token
steps.lede: The SPA calls the resource server with the access token it parsed from the fragment — the same value that sat in the URL. There is no sender constraint: anyone who read the fragment can replay this exact header.
steps.devtools: Filter on resource. The Authorization: Bearer header is the same token that was in the URL fragment. It is a pure bearer credential — no sender constraint — so an attacker who obtained the fragment (history sync, injected script, leaked link) can replay it and the API cannot tell them apart.

steps.label: Why this flow is deprecated
steps.lede: Tokens in the URL, no /token call, no client authentication: whoever obtains the fragment can replay the access token, and there is no in-protocol mitigation. This is what deprecated implicit.
steps.devtools: The fragment lands in browser history, is exposed to any injected script via location.hash, and can leak via referrer edge cases. Theft is undetectable because the token has no sender constraint. The fix is not a patch — migrate to Authorization Code + PKCE.

steps.label: Silent renewal (no refresh token)
steps.lede: Implicit issues no refresh token, so renewal happens only via a hidden iframe re-running /authorize with prompt=none. Under blocked third-party cookies this returns error=login_required, forcing a full interactive redirect.
steps.devtools: Filter on authorize again — a hidden iframe with prompt=none. On modern browsers that block third-party cookies the response fragment carries #error=login_required, so the SPA must fall back to a full interactive redirect. This renewal fragility is another reason implicit is hard to keep alive.
